title: NimbleBrain Host Extension
description: Schema for the `ai.nimblebrain/host` MCP `_meta` extension — how an MCP server declares its UI integration (placements, hooks, notifications, lifecycle) in the NimbleBrain host shell. Carried in the server's descriptor `_meta`, which for this host is the connector catalog's ServerDetail entry. The `ui://` app resources themselves are standard MCP Apps; this extension only declares where they are placed.

host_version.description: Host extension contract major version. Write "1.0". It changes only on a breaking change; adding a block does not bump it, and a block is enabled by being present, never by this value. Any "1.x" (and "1") is major 1. The host drops a catalog entry whose host_version is not major 1, since that is a contract it predates. Within major 1 the host is FORWARD-COMPATIBLE, and this tolerance is part of the contract: it parses the fields it understands and ignores the rest; unknown top-level keys validate and are ignored; an unknown or malformed placement slot drops only that placement, never the whole declaration.

placements.description: Shell layout placement declarations. Several `sidebar.<group>` placements from one server are one app in the sidebar: it is listed once under the catalog entry's `title`, opens its first placement by priority, and lists the placements beneath it by `label` while one is open.

hooks.description: Inbound event streams this server accepts, one entry per vendor. READ FROM A CATALOG CONNECTOR ONLY — the host resolves hooks from the operator-published connector catalog, never from an MCPB bundle manifest, because the route and registration tool decide where a delivery is sent and must come from operator-trusted metadata. Declaring hooks in an MCPB manifest has no effect. The host mints a capability URL per (workspace, connector, vendor) when the server is installed, hands it to the declared register_tool, and forwards deliveries to that URL verbatim to the declared route on this same server — body bytes unchanged, the vendor's own headers passed through. The host never parses a delivery body: signature verification, parsing, idempotency and state are entirely the server's.

admin_tools.description: Bare names of tools on THIS server that only a workspace admin may call. READ FROM A CATALOG CONNECTOR ONLY, like hooks: never from an MCPB bundle manifest and never from a tool's own _meta or anything else the running server sends, so a later build cannot widen access by dropping it. It only narrows: on every door (chat, the MCP endpoint, the app bridge, REST, tasks and other unattended runs) the host removes these tools from the listings of anyone who is not a workspace admin and refuses them at dispatch with the structured error workspace_admin_required. Workspace admin means a member of the bound workspace whose membership role is admin; an org admin who is not that gets no bypass, and a caller with no identity is refused. Enforced by name whether or not the server advertises the tool; an unadvertised name is an install warning. A present value that is not a list of at most 64 such names (null included) gates EVERY tool on this server, since dropping any part of a narrowing list would widen access; duplicate names only collapse. The host's own calls to this server's lifecycle handlers and hooks register_tool are not checked; naming one of those here is an install warning. Personal (identity-plane) connectors are not gated: they act on their owner's own account. This gates WHO calls, not whether a human is present: an admin's own agent passes, so an admin-only tool must still be safe for that agent to call.

HookDeclaration.description: One inbound event stream. This is the entire vendor-specific configuration the host ever sees — a name, a route, a tool, and prose. It deliberately cannot describe payload shapes or event taxonomies.

vendor.description: Vendor slug, lowercase alphanumeric with internal hyphens. Appears as a path segment in the minted URL and is sealed into its token, so the two are cross-checked on every delivery. One entry per vendor: a duplicate is dropped.

route.description: Absolute path ON THIS SERVER that a delivery is forwarded to, e.g. "/ingest/acme". Resolved against this server's own base URL and refused if it resolves to a different origin, so it may not be protocol-relative ("//host"), contain "..", a backslash, a fragment, or control characters. It may not be this server's MCP endpoint path or a path under it; such a hook is refused at install and at delivery.

register_tool.description: Name of a tool on THIS server that the host calls with { vendor, url } — both strings — to hand over the minted URL. The tool must exist on the server's tools/list at install time AND accept those two arguments. If it does not, no URL is minted for any of this server's streams and the operator is shown a warning naming the declaration — the connector still installs and its tools still work. The check re-runs whenever the connection is re-established, so fixing the manifest and reconnecting provisions the streams without a reinstall. Typically the server stores the URL in its own operator-writable config and registers it with the vendor.

description.description: Human-readable summary of what this stream carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

header_renames.description: Rename inbound headers before the forward, as { from: to }. The forward strips the header class a caller could use to assert identity (authorization, x-api-key, x-tenant-id, x-workspace-id, …) — the same class the fleet edge strips — and the browser's session credential, cookie. A vendor that authenticates its deliveries on one of the identity headers cannot otherwise reach its own verifier, so declaring a rename moves the value to a header the strip list does not cover. cookie cannot be renamed through: no vendor signs a delivery with it, so a rename from cookie is ignored. A rename whose target is itself in the stripped class is ignored.

NotificationsDeclaration.description: The outbox this server exposes — one MCP resource the host reads on a schedule for facts nobody asked for (a domain went active, a reply landed). The host reads it as the RFC 6570 template <resource>{?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} and expects the MCP Triggers-and-Events poll result { events, cursor, truncated, hasMore, nextPollMs }. Declaring an outbox grants NO privilege: nothing is minted, no new token audience exists, and no path to a human is opened — a workspace admin's route does that. What it does impose is cost, a standing poll per (workspace, connector), which the host bounds with its own cadence floor, backoff and per-workspace budget.

resource.description: The outbox resource URI, e.g. "acme://notifications". Scheme and path are both the server's own. Three rules bind. It must carry a scheme. It must NOT carry a query string or a fragment, because the host appends {?cursor,maxEvents,maxAgeMs} itself and a server-supplied query would either be overwritten or produce two. And its scheme must not be one the host resolves itself — skill://, ui://, artifact://, files://, app:// — because a single resource cannot mean two things to the same reader; such a declaration is refused and the outbox is never polled.

description.description: What the outbox carries. Operator-facing only — the host never acts on it.

slot.description: Shell slot to fill: "sidebar" (core nav), "sidebar.<group>" (the workspace's apps, e.g. "sidebar.apps"), "sidebar.bottom" (pinned), "main" (page content), or "settings": the component rendered on the connector's settings page. Claims no navigation. The host renders the first by priority; `route` and `label` are ignored. Unknown slots are dropped by the host, never fatal.

resourceUri.description: ui:// resource URI served by this MCP server.

priority.description: Sort order within the slot. Lower values appear first. Default: 100.

label.description: Human-readable label for sidebar items and tabs.

icon.description: Lucide icon name (kebab-case). Shown on a `sidebar.bottom` entry; a connector's other sidebar entries show its catalog `icons`.

route.description: Route path. Registers as /app/<path>. A route belongs to one server, compared ignoring case, percent-encoding and repeated, leading or trailing slashes: a placement whose route is one of the host's own views, or one another connector in the workspace registered first, is dropped with a logged warning.

size.description: Size hint for the slot renderer.
